text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: auth anomaly detected — spike of failed logins against /v1/login from 192.0.2.0/24 (fail rate 78% over 5m). Possible credential-spray. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/2345

Alex M: Ack, I'm oncall. marking P1 and joining. collecting traces now. :eyes:

Jay (sre): seeing same. auth-service 401s, not 5xx. quick grep from auth logs:
```
2026-03-15T22:04:02Z auth svc login failed user=unknown ip=192.0.2.18 method=POST path=/v1/login status=401 reason=invalid_credentials
2026-03-15T22:04:03Z auth svc login failed user=unknown ip=192.0.2.45 method=POST path=/v1/login status=401 reason=invalid_credentials
```

Maria (sec): enrichment: source IPs span 3 ASNs, repetitive user-agent patterns, many attempts per IP. Looks like automated spray vs targeted exfil. Recommend immediate rate-limit + blocklist on offending CIDRs. WAF rule to drop suspicious UA patterns.

Priya (support): CS intake: two enterprise customers reported mass failed logins and temporary lockouts. No confirmed account compromises yet. They want a status note for their security teams.

Alex M: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) apply short-term global rate-limit on /v1/login (burst 10 -> 2 requests/s) 2) block 192.0.2.0/24 and any other high-volume CIDRs for 1h 3) enable WAF rule for known bad UA signatures 4) rotate any service tokens that show suspicious usage. Agree?

Jay (sre): I'm pushing a nginx limit_req for /v1/login and adding IP deny on edge. Commands I'm applying now:
```
# add iptables block
sudo ipset create tmp-block hash:net || true
sudo ipset add tmp-block 192.0.2.0/24
iptables -I INPUT -m set --match-set tmp-block src -j DROP

# nginx rate limit for login
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=login:10m rate=2r/s;
location /v1/login {
  limit_req zone=login burst=10 nodelay;
}
```

deploy-bot: WAF rule 9876 deployed to prod (rule: block UA regex /^(curl|massbot)/i) — rollout 100% in 30s. :white_check_mark:

Maria (sec): I started an IP enrichment job, collecting historical hits for those IPs. Also flagging any long-lived tokens created around 2026-03-14 as suspicious. If we see service tokens used from that range, rotate them asap.

Alex M: Priya, can you draft a one-paragraph customer advisory for affected tenants? Keep it factual: we detected automated login attempts, we've applied rate limits and blocks, please reset creds if you see suspicious activity. We'll share updates in 1h.

Priya (support): Draft ready, posting to affected customer orgs now. also opening support tickets for the two customers who reported lockouts.

Jay (sre): Running quick scan for tokens with auth events from 192.0.2.0/24 in the last 48h. If any service account usage found, run rotate-key.sh with --id <key-id> --reason "suspicious-origin". Example:
```
./tools/rotate-key.sh --id svc-auth-2025 --env prod --reason suspicious-origin
```

Maria (sec): I'm triggering the key-rotation playbook for any tokens flagged. Logging actions to secure-audit. Also starting a live capture for the next 2h for further analysis.

Alex M: Temporary mitigation summary for handoff:
- Rate limit on /v1/login applied (2r/s)
- Blocklist applied: 192.0.2.0/24 (ipset+iptables)
- WAF UA block deployed
- CS notified affected customers, tickets opened
- SRE scanning/rotating suspicious service keys

Lina (pm): Filing incident ticket (INC-2026-2345) with impact: "partial login disruption for ~2 customers, automated credential spray detected; mitigations in place." Will schedule follow-up postmortem tomorrow.

Alex M: Handing this to night oncall Sara (Sara (oncall-night)). Sara — full status above, logs & rotate notes are in the incident doc. If anything escalates, page SRE escalation channel.

Sara (oncall-night): Acknowledged. I'll monitor dashboards and keep the blocklist for 1h unless we see collateral damage. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Note: key-rotation activity logged at 2345678940 by Jay (sre).

Alex M: Closing active paging loop from primary oncall. Leave monitoring and tickets open. We'll reconvene for postmortem/CTI in the morning. :lock:
